explain.say: Here's an amazing thing: a glass bottle can be recycled again and again, without wearing out! Let's follow one round the cycle on the board. It starts when you drop an empty jar or bottle into a bottle bank.

explain.say: See the eye? At the plant, glass is sorted by colour: clear, green and brown. Melted glass keeps its colour, so mixing would make muddy-coloured bottles. Machines also pick out lids, labels and stones. What colour are most bottles in your kitchen?

explain.say: Look at the rock. The glass is crushed into small, gritty pieces called cullet. Then, at the fire, the cullet goes into a furnace at about 1,500 degrees with sand and other minerals. Cullet melts more easily than sand, so it saves energy.

explain.say: See the factory? Glowing blobs of melted glass drop into moulds, and air blows them into a bottle shape, like blowing up a balloon inside a box. Then they're cooled slowly so they don't crack. How long do you think until it's back in a shop?

explain.say: As little as a month! Look: back on the shop shelf, and round the cycle again. Well done! Wow: glass is made mostly from sand, and some of the oldest glass beads, from Egypt and Mesopotamia, are over 4,000 years old. Challenge: rinse a jar and recycle it this week!

faq.q: Why is glass sorted by colour?
faq.a: Glass keeps its colour when it's melted. To make clear bottles you need clear glass, so clear, green and brown glass are kept apart.
asks: Can different coloured glass be recycled together?

faq.q: Why does recycled glass save energy?
faq.a: Crushed old glass, called cullet, melts at a lower temperature than the raw sand mix, so furnaces use less fuel. It also saves digging up new sand.
Yes. Glass bottles and jars can be melted and remade over and over without losing quality.
asks: How many times can glass be recycled?

faq.a: Mostly sand, which is silica, melted with soda ash and limestone at very high temperatures.

faq.q: Can I recycle drinking glasses with bottles?
faq.a: Usually not. Drinking glasses, windows and ovenproof dishes are made differently and melt at other temperatures, so they can spoil a batch of bottle glass.
asks: Why can't I recycle a broken drinking glass?

facts: Glass containers can be recycled endlessly without loss of quality.
Crushed recycled glass, called cullet, melts at a lower temperature than raw materials, which saves energy.
